issue.body:
### Elasticsearch Version

main (9.7.0-SNAPSHOT). Affects 9.2+ for `CATEGORIZE` and 9.5+ for `ST_BUFFER`.

### Problem Description

When a function runs on an older data node, some of its options are not sent to it. The older node runs the function with default options, and the response looks complete (`is_partial: false`, no warning).

Confirmed for:
- `CATEGORIZE` `similarity_threshold` on 9.1 nodes. `analyzer` is probably affected too (not tested). `output_format` is fine because it is applied on the coordinator.
- `ST_BUFFER` options (e.g. `quad_segs`) on 9.4 nodes, when buffering a field. A constant geometry is buffered on the coordinator and is not affected.

This affects mixed clusters during a rolling upgrade, and CCS to an older remote.

`Categorize#writeTo` and `StBuffer#writeTo` skip `options` when the receiving node doesn't support `esql_categorize_options` / `esql_st_buffer_options`, and nothing rejects the query during planning.

**Expected:** correct results, or a 4xx saying a participating node doesn't support the options. Runtime `MATCH` options get a planning-time check in `LogicalVerifier` for this (#164734); `ToText#writeTo` throws instead.

### Steps to Reproduce

Mixed cluster with current and older nodes. Two identical indices: `*_cur` allocated to current nodes, `*_old` allocated to old nodes (`index.routing.allocation.include._name`). Queries are sent to a current node.

`CATEGORIZE`, old nodes on 9.1.9, `message` is `text` with five lines: `Connected to 10.1.0.1`, `Connected to 10.1.0.2`, `Connection error on host 10.1.0.3`, `Disconnected from 10.1.0.1`, `Disconnected from 10.1.0.2`:
```
FROM logs_cur | STATS c = COUNT(*) BY category = CATEGORIZE(message, {"similarity_threshold": 99}) | SORT category
FROM logs_old | STATS c = COUNT(*) BY category = CATEGORIZE(message, {"similarity_threshold": 99}) | SORT category
```

`ST_BUFFER`, old nodes on 9.4.9, `pt` is a `geo_point` (`POINT(10 10)`, `POINT(20 20)`):
```
FROM shapes_cur | EVAL n = LENGTH(TO_STRING(ST_BUFFER(pt, 1.0, {"quad_segs": 1}))) | WHERE n > 0 | KEEP id, n | SORT id
FROM shapes_old | EVAL n = LENGTH(TO_STRING(ST_BUFFER(pt, 1.0, {"quad_segs": 1}))) | WHERE n > 0 | KEEP id, n | SORT id
```

| | Shards on current nodes | Shards on old nodes |
|---|---|---|
| `CATEGORIZE` categories | 5 | 3 (same as default threshold) |
| `ST_BUFFER` WKT length | 198, 195 | 1250, 1272 (same as default `quad_segs`) |

All responses are 200 with `is_partial: false`.

### Logs (if relevant)

None. No errors or warnings are logged.

issue.body:
### Elasticsearch Version

main (9.7.0-SNAPSHOT, 99c5e08e2822); also affects the unreleased 9.6.0 (`9.6` branch).
No released version is affected yet.

### Installed Plugins

None (default distribution)

### Java Version

_bundled_

### OS Version

N/A

### Problem Description

When a 9.6 coordinator runs a runtime `MATCH` or `MATCH_PHRASE` with options, any 9.5 node that executes part of the plan ignores those options, so results are silently wrong.
A runtime search is one whose field argument is an expression or another non-indexed value, for example `MATCH(TO_LOWER(title), "quick fox", {"operator": "AND"})`.
This affects CCS from 9.6 to a 9.5 remote and 9.5/9.6 mixed clusters during a rolling upgrade.

**Expected:** the query either honours the options on every node, or fails with a 4xx that says a participating node does not support them.

**Actual:** 9.5 nodes run the search with default options.
No error or warning is returned.
For example, `operator: AND` becomes `OR` (more rows match), and `fuzziness`, `minimum_should_match`, `analyzer` and `lenient` are silently ignored.

**Root cause:**
- Options on runtime searches were added in 9.6 (#154718 for `MATCH`, #155315 for `MATCH_PHRASE`, #155554 for `analyzer`). Their serialization (#154382) is gated on the `esql_options_for_search_functions` transport version, which does not exist on 9.5.
- [`Match#writeTo`](https://github.com/elastic/elasticsearch/blob/99c5e08e2822745dccf018ab0a047dd83a0e2bde/x-pack/plugin/esql/src/main/java/org/elasticsearch/xpack/esql/expression/function/fulltext/Match.java#L362-L370) and [`MatchPhrase#writeTo`](https://github.com/elastic/elasticsearch/blob/99c5e08e2822745dccf018ab0a047dd83a0e2bde/x-pack/plugin/esql/src/main/java/org/elasticsearch/xpack/esql/expression/function/fulltext/MatchPhrase.java#L237-L246) skip `options()` for older receivers.
- For indexed fields that loss is harmless. [`QueryBuilderResolver`](https://github.com/elastic/elasticsearch/blob/99c5e08e2822745dccf018ab0a047dd83a0e2bde/x-pack/plugin/esql/src/main/java/org/elasticsearch/xpack/esql/expression/function/fulltext/QueryBuilderResolver.java#L124-L137) builds the `QueryBuilder` on the coordinator, and that builder carries the options to older nodes.
- Runtime searches have no `QueryBuilder`, because [`FullTextFunction#requiresQueryBuilderRewrite`](https://github.com/elastic/elasticsearch/blob/99c5e08e2822745dccf018ab0a047dd83a0e2bde/x-pack/plugin/esql/src/main/java/org/elasticsearch/xpack/esql/expression/function/fulltext/FullTextFunction.java#L817-L819) returns `false` for them. So the serialized `options` are the only way options reach the data node.
- Runtime `MATCH` itself exists on 9.5.0 (capability `match_runtime_search`), so a 9.5 node does not fail: it runs the search with default options.
- Runtime `KNN` has the same exposure and is protected by [`LogicalVerifier#checkKnnRuntimeSearchSupported`](https://github.com/elastic/elasticsearch/blob/99c5e08e2822745dccf018ab0a047dd83a0e2bde/x-pack/plugin/esql/src/main/java/org/elasticsearch/xpack/esql/optimizer/LogicalVerifier.java#L76-L91), which fails fast with a 4xx when the minimum transport version is too old. Runtime `MATCH` / `MATCH_PHRASE` options have no such check.

**Proposed fix:** in `LogicalVerifier`, fail with a 4xx when a runtime `Match` or `MatchPhrase` has non-null options and the minimum transport version does not support `ESQL_OPTIONS_FOR_SEARCH_FUNCTIONS`. Follow the pattern of `checkKnnRuntimeSearchSupported`.

Related:
- #154718: allows options for runtime `MATCH`.
- #155315: options for runtime `MATCH_PHRASE`.
- #155554: `analyzer` option on runtime `MATCH`.
- #154382: serializes search function options behind the new transport version.
- #161205: adds the equivalent minimum-version check for runtime `KNN`.

Found by code inspection; not yet reproduced on a real CCS or mixed-version cluster.

### Steps to Reproduce

Requires a 9.6 local cluster with a 9.5 remote cluster registered as `remote_95`.

On the 9.5 remote:

```
PUT books
{
  "mappings": {
    "properties": {
      "title": { "type": "text" }
    }
  }
}

POST books/_bulk?refresh=true
{"index": {"_id": "1"}}
{"title": "The Quick Brown Fox"}
{"index": {"_id": "2"}}
{"title": "A Quick Dog"}
```

On the 9.6 local cluster:

```
POST _query
{
  "query": "FROM remote_95:books | EVAL t = TO_LOWER(title) | WHERE MATCH(t, \"quick fox\", {\"operator\": \"AND\"}) | KEEP title"
}
# Expected: only "The Quick Brown Fox", or a 4xx saying the remote does not support the options.
# Actual: both rows are returned, because the 9.5 remote runs the match with operator OR.
```

Control: running the same query against a 9.6 remote, or on `title` directly (an indexed-field match), returns only "The Quick Brown Fox".
The same applies to `MATCH_PHRASE(t, "...", {"slop": 2})` and to a mixed cluster where some shards of `books` sit on 9.5 nodes.

### Logs (if relevant)

_No response_

comment.body:
Yeah for runtime `MATCH_PHRASE` we won't get silently inconsistent results. We will get shard failures for 9.5 nodes though, since they don't have runtime match. (I think the same for runtime `MATCH` on 9.4)

So in an upgrade scenario for example where 4 shards are in old nodes and 4 in new, it would look something like

issue.body:
QSTR documents a `fields` option but rejects it, e.g. `QSTR("hello", {"fields": ["title"]})` fails with `Invalid option [fields]`.

Allowing the key isn't enough on its own. The generic options handling turns every value into a single string, and `translate()` never passes any fields to the query, so `fields` is now read separately from the option literal and set as the fields of the `query_string` query.

How it behaves:
- `fields` takes a list or a single string, e.g. `{"fields": ["title^2", "desc*"]}` or `{"fields": "title"}`. Boosts and wildcards work the same as in the DSL (same parser).
- `fields` together with `default_field` is a verification error. The `query_string` query rejects that combination anyway, but only on the shard.
- Invalid or negative boosts (`title^high`, `title^-1`) are verification errors too.
- New `fn_qstr_fields_option` capability.

Tests: verifier tests for the accepted forms and the errors, a pushdown test checking the fields and boosts on the `QueryStringQueryBuilder`, csv-spec tests on `books` that only pass if `fields` is applied, and a check that every documented full-text `@MapParam` option is in `ALLOWED_OPTIONS`.

Closes #162643

issue.body:
A `text` field searched from its values rather than from an index of its terms — a columnar field
with `index: false`, a runtime column, an external dataset — has to analyze every document, because
the values are the only record of the tokens they hold.

A token is a stretch of the value, spelled the way the value spells it. So a value spelling none of
the query's terms cannot analyze into them. This reads the bytes first, with the folded compare from
#162156, and analyzes only what is left.

It errs one way. A value the read keeps is analyzed exactly as before and answered by that; the read
answers a value itself only to rule it out, or, where a match sits between two token boundaries, to
accept it. Nothing about the score moves: a query walked over a value's tokens reports the frequency
and the clause count an index of the same values reports, and randomised tests hold both against a
`MemoryIndex`.

The read is given up for the query, never for the corpus: an analyzer outside the allowlist
(`standard`, `whitespace`, `simple`, `stop`, `keyword` — each cuts its input into stretches of
itself and at most lowercases or drops them, whatever its configuration, and all five are final), a
clause naming a range of terms rather than the terms themselves, or a term spelled more ways than
the cap allows. Nothing about the values turns it off.

### The commits

- **Rule out a value before analyzing it** — the rule, with no caller yet. What a query requires of
  a value comes from whichever shape the caller holds it in; the analyzer decides whether the values
  can be read for it at all.
- **Analyze only the values that could hold the tokens** — three call sites: the Lucene query over a
  columnar field's column, ES|QL's per-value matcher, and ES|QL's per-row `MemoryIndex` path.
- **Walk a term as the phrase of one it is** — a phrase already answers itself by walking the tokens
  of a value; a term is a phrase of one, so it walks too instead of indexing the document.
- **Walk the clauses of a query over its values** — the same for a query of several terms, each
  clause answered by any of the terms it names.
- **Answer a value by where its tokens end** — a match between two boundaries is the token, so the
  value is answered yes and never analyzed; a match whose neighbour continues a token is no match, so
  `cat` in `catalog` is answered no. The yes is taken narrowly: ASCII only, and only where holding
  the term settles the document's score.

### Numbers

One node, one shard force-merged, 7,320 Wikipedia articles — 283 MB of column — in a `columnar`
index whose `body` is `text` with `index: false`. `took` in ms, median of 7 runs after 2 warmups,
request cache off. Both arms answer the same documents, which every row asserts.

| query                           | main  | this branch |        |
|---------------------------------|-------|-------------|--------|
| 1 term, rare                    | 7,965 |     **414** | 19.2x  |
| 2 terms, all of them            | 8,355 |     **498** | 16.8x  |
| a phrase of 2                   | 4,372 |     **477** |  9.2x  |
| 1 term, common                  | 8,512 |   **1,288** |  6.6x  |
| 8 terms, any of them            | 8,197 |   **5,425** |  1.51x |
| 17 terms, any of them, over the cap | 8,205 | **5,076** |  1.62x |

Where few documents hold the terms the read answers the query almost alone. Where nearly all of them
do it has nothing to rule out and the token walk is the gain, which is the last two rows — the query
of 17 terms is over the read's cap, so it declines entirely. Medians move by 20 to 30 percent between
restarts of the node, so the columns are read against each other within a run rather than across
runs.

Reading the column is now the larger half of a selective query: of the 521 ms a rare term takes,
about 460 ms is the column read and decode and about 60 ms is answering the query.

### Still indexed a document at a time

A clause naming a range of terms rather than the terms themselves (a fuzziness, a prefix, a phrase
prefix, a wildcard), a phrase with slop or non-consecutive positions, a phrase clause inside a
boolean, a blended query over several fields, and a query two of whose clauses name the same terms.

issue.body:
Closes #163537

`text` and `match_only_text` fields searched from their values (`index: false` in a columnar index) wrap their analysed boolean query in a `ReanalyzingTextQuery`; `match_only_text` also wraps that in a `ConstantScoreQuery`. `Queries.maybeApplyMinimumShouldMatch` only handled a top-level `BooleanQuery`, so `query_string` and `simple_query_string` silently dropped `minimum_should_match` on these fields and returned more documents than an indexed field would.

### Changes
- `Queries.maybeApplyMinimumShouldMatch` now applies msm to the boolean inside `ReanalyzingTextQuery(BooleanQuery)` and `ConstantScoreQuery(ReanalyzingTextQuery(BooleanQuery))`, then wraps it again. The constant-score case only unwraps when the wrapper is directly inside, so `ConstantScoreQuery(BooleanQuery)` from other field types is left alone as before.
- New `ReanalyzingTextQuery.withQuery(Query)` builds the rewrapped copy.
- Removed the parser-level msm handling in `MatchQueryParser` and its setter calls in `MatchQueryBuilder`, `MatchBoolPrefixQueryBuilder` and `MultiMatchQueryParser`. Every builder applies msm after parsing, so it was redundant.

### Tests
- `QueriesTests`: unwrap, rewrap, no-op cases, and that `withQuery` keeps `scansEveryDocument`.
- `TextNoTermsSearchTests` and `MatchOnlyTextNoTermsSearchTests`: `query_string`, `simple_query_string`, `match`, `multi_match` and `match_bool_prefix` with msm (including boosted variants), each compared between an indexed and an `index: false` field. The new cases fail without the fix.

### Note for #162005
That PR adds a `valuesAnalyzer` field to `ReanalyzingTextQuery`. Whichever change merges second must pass it through in `withQuery`, otherwise msm queries quietly lose the fast read.

issue.body:
### Summary
On a columnar index, `text` and `match_only_text` fields with `index: false` ignore `minimum_should_match` in some queries. Those queries then behave like a plain OR, and return documents that the same query on an indexed field would not return.

### Reproduction
A columnar index with `body` mapped as `text` and `"index": false`, and these documents:

```
0: "the quick brown fox jumps"
1: "brown the quick fox"
2: "quick brown"
3: "nothing here at all"
```

```json
{ "query_string": { "query": "quick nothing", "default_field": "body", "minimum_should_match": 2 } }
```

| Mapping | Hits |
|---|---|
| `"index": true` | none (no document has both words) |
| `"index": false` | 0, 1, 2, 3 |

### Affected queries
| Field | Query | Affected |
|---|---|---|
| `text` | `query_string` | yes |
| `text` | `simple_query_string`, when one word splits into several tokens (e.g. `quick-nothing`) | yes |
| `text` | `match`, `multi_match`, `match_bool_prefix` | no |
| `match_only_text` | `query_string`, `simple_query_string` (same cases as above) | yes |

### Cause
When a field is searched from its values, `MatchQueryParser` wraps the analysed boolean query in a `ReanalyzingTextQuery`; `match_only_text` also wraps that in a `ConstantScoreQuery`. `Queries.maybeApplyMinimumShouldMatch` only applies msm to a top-level `BooleanQuery`, so on a wrapped query it does nothing.

`match`, `multi_match` and `match_bool_prefix` avoid this because the parser applies msm before wrapping. `query_string` and `simple_query_string` can't do the same: their msm applies to the query they assemble from several parsed pieces, which only exists after parsing.

### Proposed fix
- Have `Queries.maybeApplyMinimumShouldMatch` look through the wrapper, both `ReanalyzingTextQuery(BooleanQuery)` and `ConstantScoreQuery(ReanalyzingTextQuery(BooleanQuery))`: apply msm to the inner boolean, then wrap it again. This fixes every caller in one place.
- Remove the parser's own msm handling, which this makes redundant.
- Add tests to `TextNoTermsSearchTests` and `MatchOnlyTextNoTermsSearchTests` that compare indexed and `index: false` results for each query type with msm.

issue.body:
### Summary
On a columnar index, `text` and `match_only_text` fields with `index: false` ignore `minimum_should_match` in some queries. Those queries then behave like a plain OR, and return documents that the same query on an indexed field would not return.

### Reproduction
A columnar index with `body` mapped as `text` and `"index": false`, and these documents:

```
0: "the quick brown fox jumps"
1: "brown the quick fox"
2: "quick brown"
3: "nothing here at all"
```

```json
{ "query_string": { "query": "quick nothing", "default_field": "body", "minimum_should_match": 2 } }
```

| Mapping | Hits |
|---|---|
| `"index": true` | none (no document has both words) |
| `"index": false` | 0, 1, 2, 3 |

### Affected queries
| Field | Query | Affected |
|---|---|---|
| `text` | `query_string` | yes |
| `text` | `simple_query_string`, when one word splits into several tokens (e.g. `quick-nothing`) | yes |
| `text` | `match`, `multi_match`, `match_bool_prefix` | no |
| `match_only_text` | `query_string`, `simple_query_string` (same cases as above) | yes |

### Cause
When a field is searched from its values, `MatchQueryParser` wraps the analysed boolean query in a `ReanalyzingTextQuery`; `match_only_text` also wraps that in a `ConstantScoreQuery`. `Queries.maybeApplyMinimumShouldMatch` only applies msm to a top-level `BooleanQuery`, so on a wrapped query it does nothing.

### Proposed fix
- Have `Queries.maybeApplyMinimumShouldMatch` look through the wrapper, both `ReanalyzingTextQuery(BooleanQuery)` and `ConstantScoreQuery(ReanalyzingTextQuery(BooleanQuery))`: apply msm to the inner boolean, then wrap it again. This fixes every caller in one place.
- Remove the parser's own msm handling, which this makes redundant.
- Add tests to `TextNoTermsSearchTests` and `MatchOnlyTextNoTermsSearchTests` that compare indexed and `index: false` results for each query type with msm.

issue.body:
### Description

A `_search` request that uses the `suggest_field` URL parameter without `suggest_mode` fails with a 500 `NullPointerException`. The documented default for the term suggester `suggest_mode` is `missing`, so the request should succeed. If the parameter is required, the API should return a 400, not a 500.

### Steps to reproduce

```
GET /<index>/_search?suggest_field=message&suggest_text=abc
```

The `suggest_size` parameter already has a default (5), but `suggest_mode` does not.

### Actual behavior

This was raised as a serverless suppressed rest exception alert. Search slack for this issues URL to find the original alert.

HTTP 500. The `rest.suppressed` logger records:

```
path: /<index>/_search, params: {suggest_field=message, suggest_text=abc, index=<index>, serverlessRequest=true}, status: 500
```

```
java.lang.NullPointerException: Input string is null
	at java.base/java.util.Objects.requireNonNull(Objects.java:246)
	at org.elasticsearch.server@9.6.0/org.elasticsearch.search.suggest.term.TermSuggestionBuilder$SuggestMode.resolve(TermSuggestionBuilder.java:530)
	at org.elasticsearch.server@9.6.0/org.elasticsearch.rest.action.search.RestSearchAction.parseSuggestUrlParameters(RestSearchAction.java:426)
	at org.elasticsearch.server@9.6.0/org.elasticsearch.rest.action.search.RestSearchAction.parseSearchSource(RestSearchAction.java:405)
	at org.elasticsearch.server@9.6.0/org.elasticsearch.rest.action.search.RestSearchAction.parseSearchRequest(RestSearchAction.java:272)
	at org.elasticsearch.server@9.6.0/org.elasticsearch.rest.action.search.RestSearchAction.lambda$prepareRequest$1(RestSearchAction.java:137)
	at org.elasticsearch.server@9.6.0/org.elasticsearch.rest.RestRequest.withContentOrSourceParamParserOrNull(RestRequest.java:644)
	at org.elasticsearch.server@9.6.0/org.elasticsearch.rest.action.search.RestSearchAction.prepareRequest(RestSearchAction.java:136)
	at org.elasticsearch.server@9.6.0/org.elasticsearch.rest.BaseRestHandler.handleRequest(BaseRestHandler.java:99)
	(remaining frames omitted)
```

### Expected behavior

The request succeeds with `suggest_mode` defaulting to `missing`.

### Cause

`RestSearchAction.parseSuggestUrlParameters` reads the parameter with `request.param("suggest_mode")`, which returns `null` when the parameter is absent. It passes the value to `TermSuggestionBuilder.SuggestMode.resolve`, and that method calls `Objects.requireNonNull`.

### Suggested fix

Read the parameter with a default, `request.param("suggest_mode", "missing")`. Add a unit test in `RestSearchActionTests` for `suggest_field` without `suggest_mode`.

### Version

Seen on Elasticsearch Serverless (build 9.6.0). It is not yet checked whether older versions are affected.

issue.body:
The `Index Sort` test force merges to a single segment and then checks `_doc` order, which only works if the copy we search is actually that one merged segment. The health check after creating the index waits for no initializing shards, but that also passes while the replica is still unassigned. If the replica then gets assigned while we are indexing, it can still be recovering when the force merge runs, the merge skips it, and a search that lands on it returns docs out of index sort order (1,2,4,3 in the failure). This shows up mostly in the mixed cluster BWC runs since there are 4 nodes and more room for the replica to be late.

I first pinned `number_of_replicas: 0` like #160246 did for `340_flattened`, but that breaks serverless: stateless needs a replica to search on, so every search failed with no shard available (`340_flattened` only got away with it because serverless skips that test). 

So instead the index uses `auto_expand_replicas: 0-1` and the health check also waits for green. That gives 
- Single node: 0 replicas, so green is reachable.
- Multi-node: 1 replica, which must be started before indexing, so the force merge reaches both copies.
- Serverless: always at least 1 replica (AutoExpandReplicas.java:160), so searches have a shard again.

`30_multi_value` has the same setup and was muted for the same kind of failure, made the same change for that along with the unmutes (#154602, #161280, #163014).

`40_high_cardinality` and `340_flattened` get the same change, as a precaution and to keep the setup consistent.

>  Testing:  
>- The race didn't reproduce on its own locally (100 iterations with the failure seed), so I forced it with a scratch copy of the test: hold the replica back until after the health check, flush a large doc and throttle recovery so it's still running during the force merge. With the old health check it failed 5/5 with the same 1,2,4,3 order as CI, with the new one it passed 5/5.
> - `:rest-api-spec:yamlRestTest` for `indices.sort`, and `:qa:mixed-cluster:v9.3.8#yamlRestTest` for `Index Sort` (20 iterations).
> - Serverless `:qa:core-rest-test:yamlRestTest` and `yamlRestTestWithMultiProject` for `indices.sort` against this branch: the 5 no shard available failures from CI before the change, all green after (10 iterations).


The mute for this test only exists on 9.5 (#162592), so the backport should remove it there.

Closes #162591
Closes #154602
Closes #161280
Closes #163014

issue.body:
## Problem

`binary`, `text` and `match_only_text` default to `doc_values` disabled with high cardinality (`DISABLED_HIGH_CARDINALITY`, see `BinaryFieldMapper`, `TextFieldMapper`, `MatchOnlyTextFieldMapper`). `DocValuesParameter#parse` in `FieldMapper` turns an explicit `"doc_values": false` into `DISABLED_LOW_CARDINALITY`. Cardinality means nothing when doc values are off, but the two values are not equal, so an explicit `false` is treated as a non-default setting.

## Impact

1. Mapping updates between `{"type": "binary"}` and `{"type": "binary", "doc_values": false}` are rejected by the cardinality check in the merge validator. The same applies to `text` and `match_only_text`. This affects upgrades from 9.5 to 9.6: 9.5 stores a mapping with `"doc_values": false` without the parameter, so re-sending the original mapping after the upgrade fails. #162142 is in 9.6, which is not released yet.
2. Since the explicit `false` now differs from the default, it is serialized. Older nodes drop it, which trips the round-trip assertion in `DocumentMapper` and crashes them in mixed-version test clusters, for example in `search/160_exists_query.yml`. This is an assertion only and has no production impact. Relates to #163053 and #162971. This does not close #163053, which also tracks a separate 9.5.6 bfloat16 recovery failure and an unrelated PR failure.

Merging mappings for `binary`, `text` and `match_only_text`:

| Existing mapping | Update | Before | After |
|---|---|---|---|
| `doc_values: false` | `doc_values: false` | OK | OK |
| omitted | `doc_values: false` | conflict | OK |
| `doc_values: false` | omitted | conflict | OK |

The conflict message was `Cannot update parameter [doc_values] from [Values[enabled=false, cardinality=high, ...]] to [Values[enabled=false, cardinality=low, ...]]`.

## Fix

When the field type's default has doc values disabled, `"doc_values": false` now resolves to that default. When the default is enabled (keyword, numbers, ip, dates and so on), it still resolves to `DISABLED_LOW_CARDINALITY`, so those mappers behave exactly as before.

I went with this rather than always using the default's cardinality. The cardinality of a disabled value is only read by the merge validator and by `toString` in conflict messages (codec selection and `usesBinaryDocValues()` check `enabled` first), so both options would work. But the deprecated `Builder.docValues(false)` helpers in `KeywordFieldMapper` and `NumberFieldMapper` set `DISABLED_LOW_CARDINALITY`, and keyword's columnar default is high cardinality, so always using the default's cardinality could introduce a similar mismatch there. `BinaryFieldMapper.Builder.docValues(false)` already uses `DISABLED_HIGH_CARDINALITY`, which now matches the parsed value.

## Testing

- Added `MapperTestCase#assertExplicitDocValuesFalseMatchesDisabledDefault`, which checks the three merges above and that `{"type": ..., "doc_values": false}` serializes without `doc_values`, as in 9.5.
- Called from new tests in `BinaryFieldMapperTests`, `TextFieldMapperTests` and `MatchOnlyTextFieldMapperTests`. All three fail on main with the conflict above and pass with the fix.
- Ran `./gradlew :server:test --tests 'org.elasticsearch.index.mapper.*'` and `./gradlew :modules:mapper-extras:test`.

This also removes the mutes for `MixedClusterClientYamlTestSuiteIT` (#163053) and `RareTermsIT` (#162971), so CI runs the suites this fixes. The v9.5.6 task can still fail intermittently on a separate bfloat16 translog assertion during recovery until #163208 is merged.

Adding `:StorageEngine/Mapping`. The periodic BWC failures (v9.0.8, v9.1.9, v9.2.8) are a mapping serialisation regression from #162142.

cc. @jimczi @martijnvg 

In those runs, both old nodes crash when a 9.7 node is master:

```
fatal error in thread [elasticsearch[test-cluster-VYpIW33O-0][clusterApplierService#updateTask][T#1]], exiting
java.lang.AssertionError: provided source [...] differs from mapping [...]
        at org.elasticsearch.index.mapper.DocumentMapper.<init>(DocumentMapper.java:72) ~[elasticsearch-9.1.9.jar:?]

sent by 9.7 master:     "binary": {"type":"binary","store":true,"doc_values":false}
re-serialised by 9.1.9: "binary": {"type":"binary","store":true}
```

(node logs from elasticsearch-periodic #12954 / 9.1.9_bwc; the mapping is from search/160_exists_query.yml). With both old nodes gone, the cluster loses its master and every remaining test fails with no master until the suite times out.

The cause is that a binary field with an explicit doc_values: false now parses to DISABLED_LOW_CARDINALITY, while the default is DISABLED_HIGH_CARDINALITY. The explicit form therefore counts as non-default and gets serialised, and older nodes drop it. The same mismatch also makes mapping updates between the explicit and omitted forms fail with a merge conflict. 

The same assertion caused #162971.

This issue also covers two failures that aren't StorageEngine's:

- v9.5.6 intake runs (the .synonyms "50% shards are active" error in the description): a 9.7 node dies on TranslogWriter.assertNoSeqNumberConflict during peer recovery. The trigger is an indexed bfloat16 vector whose source was rebuilt from the index, in search.vectors/200_dense_vector_docvalue_fields.yml. This looks like a gap in #159912, so it's for :Search Relevance/Vectors. The v9.5.6 mute here belongs to this failure, not to the mapping bug.
- v9.5.6 part_6 PR runs (Invalid magic: expected 'eirf', got 'escf'): these are all builds of the unmerged PR #162922, which turns on columnar batch indexing. The ESCF batch format has no transport version gate, so 9.5.6 nodes can't read the batches. I'll comment on that PR instead; nothing to do here.

issue.body:
Adds a per-index `index.batch_indexing` setting (final, always registered; with the `batch_indexing` feature flag off it defaults to `false` and rejects an explicit `true`) so batch indexing is opted into per index instead of only cluster-wide.

- **Default:** `true` for strictly columnar index modes, otherwise `false`. If the now-deprecated `index.time_series.batch_indexing` is explicitly set, it supplies the default.
- **Cluster setting:** `indices.batch_indexing` now defaults to the feature-flag state and acts as a kill switch.
- **Bulk routing:** `BatchModeRouter` only encodes items for indices with the setting enabled (decision cached per bulk). Items for other indices keep their inline source, so a mixed bulk still batches the eligible indices.
- **Shard level:** `ShardBatchIndexer.canUseBatchIndexing` now also requires the shard's index to have opted in, on both primary and replica.
- **Tests:** unit tests for the settings, router, shard indexer and OTLP transport action, plus an integration test in `BatchBulkIT`.

**Known temporary limitation:** the ESCF batch format does not yet preserve the original text of floating point numbers, so `CsvColumnarIT` sets `index.batch_indexing: false` on its columnar indices (see the `TODO` in `modeSettings()`). This is a limitation of the ESCF format, not of the columnar on-disk format. To be fixed in a follow-up: https://github.com/elastic/elasticsearch/issues/163401

/closes https://github.com/elastic/elasticsearch/issues/161859

issue.body:
The `Index Sort` test force merges to a single segment and then checks `_doc` order, which only works if the copy we search is actually that one merged segment. The health check after creating the index waits for no initializing shards, but that also passes while the replica is still unassigned. If the replica then gets assigned while we are indexing, it can still be recovering when the force merge runs, the merge skips it, and a search that lands on it returns docs out of index sort order (1,2,4,3 in the failure). This shows up mostly in the mixed cluster BWC runs since there are 4 nodes and more room for the replica to be late.

I first pinned `number_of_replicas: 0` like #160246 did for `340_flattened`, but that breaks serverless: stateless needs a replica to search on, so every search failed with no shard available (`340_flattened` only got away with it because serverless skips that test). 

So instead the index uses `auto_expand_replicas: 0-1` and the health check also waits for green. That gives 
- Single node: 0 replicas, so green is reachable.
- Multi-node: 1 replica, which must be started before indexing, so the force merge reaches both copies.
- Serverless: always at least 1 replica (AutoExpandReplicas.java:160), so searches have a shard again.

`30_multi_value` has the same setup and was muted for the same kind of failure, made the same change for that along with the unmutes (#154602, #161280, #163014).

`40_high_cardinality` and `340_flattened` get the same change, as a precaution and to keep the setup consistent.

>  Testing:  
>- The race didn't reproduce on its own locally (100 iterations with the failure seed), so I forced it with a scratch copy of the test: hold the replica back until after the health check, flush a large doc and throttle recovery so it's still running during the force merge. With the old health check it failed 5/5 with the same 1,2,4,3 order as CI, with the new one it passed 5/5.
> - `:rest-api-spec:yamlRestTest` for `indices.sort`, and `:qa:mixed-cluster:v9.3.8#yamlRestTest` for `Index Sort` (20 iterations).
> - Serverless `:qa:core-rest-test:yamlRestTest` and `yamlRestTestWithMultiProject` for `indices.sort` against this branch: the 5 no shard available failures from CI before the change, all green after (10 iterations).


The mute for this test only exists on 9.5 (#162592), so the backport should remove it there.

Closes #162591
Closes #154602
Closes #161280
Closes #163014

issue.body:
## Problem

`binary`, `text` and `match_only_text` default to `doc_values` disabled with high cardinality (`DISABLED_HIGH_CARDINALITY`, see `BinaryFieldMapper`, `TextFieldMapper`, `MatchOnlyTextFieldMapper`). `DocValuesParameter#parse` in `FieldMapper` turns an explicit `"doc_values": false` into `DISABLED_LOW_CARDINALITY`. Cardinality means nothing when doc values are off, but the two values are not equal, so an explicit `false` is treated as a non-default setting.

## Impact

1. Mapping updates between `{"type": "binary"}` and `{"type": "binary", "doc_values": false}` are rejected by the cardinality check in the merge validator. The same applies to `text` and `match_only_text`. This affects upgrades from 9.5 to 9.6: 9.5 stores a mapping with `"doc_values": false` without the parameter, so re-sending the original mapping after the upgrade fails. #162142 is in 9.6, which is not released yet.
2. Since the explicit `false` now differs from the default, it is serialized. Older nodes drop it, which trips the round-trip assertion in `DocumentMapper` and crashes them in mixed-version test clusters, for example in `search/160_exists_query.yml`. This is an assertion only and has no production impact. Relates to #163053 and #162971. This does not close #163053, which also tracks a separate 9.5.6 bfloat16 recovery failure and an unrelated PR failure.

Merging mappings for `binary`, `text` and `match_only_text`:

| Existing mapping | Update | Before | After |
|---|---|---|---|
| `doc_values: false` | `doc_values: false` | OK | OK |
| omitted | `doc_values: false` | conflict | OK |
| `doc_values: false` | omitted | conflict | OK |

The conflict message was `Cannot update parameter [doc_values] from [Values[enabled=false, cardinality=high, ...]] to [Values[enabled=false, cardinality=low, ...]]`.

## Fix

When the field type's default has doc values disabled, `"doc_values": false` now resolves to that default. When the default is enabled (keyword, numbers, ip, dates and so on), it still resolves to `DISABLED_LOW_CARDINALITY`, so those mappers behave exactly as before.

I went with this rather than always using the default's cardinality. The cardinality of a disabled value is only read by the merge validator and by `toString` in conflict messages (codec selection and `usesBinaryDocValues()` check `enabled` first), so both options would work. But the deprecated `Builder.docValues(false)` helpers in `KeywordFieldMapper` and `NumberFieldMapper` set `DISABLED_LOW_CARDINALITY`, and keyword's columnar default is high cardinality, so always using the default's cardinality could introduce a similar mismatch there. `BinaryFieldMapper.Builder.docValues(false)` already uses `DISABLED_HIGH_CARDINALITY`, which now matches the parsed value.

## Testing

- Added `MapperTestCase#assertExplicitDocValuesFalseMatchesDisabledDefault`, which checks the three merges above and that `{"type": ..., "doc_values": false}` serializes without `doc_values`, as in 9.5.
- Called from new tests in `BinaryFieldMapperTests`, `TextFieldMapperTests` and `MatchOnlyTextFieldMapperTests`. All three fail on main with the conflict above and pass with the fix.
- Ran `./gradlew :server:test --tests 'org.elasticsearch.index.mapper.*'` and `./gradlew :modules:mapper-extras:test`.

This also removes the mutes for `MixedClusterClientYamlTestSuiteIT` (#163053) and `RareTermsIT` (#162971), so CI runs the suites this fixes. The v9.5.6 task can still fail intermittently on a separate bfloat16 translog assertion during recovery until #163208 is merged.

issue.body: ### Elasticsearch Version 9.6.0 ### Installed Plugins _No response_ ### Java Version _bundled_ ### OS Version Darwin HW0122893 25.6.0 Darwin Kernel Version 25.6.0: Fri Jul 31 19:19:08 PDT 2026; root:xnu-12377.161.14~5/RELEASE_ARM64_T6050 arm64 ### Problem Description I am reading this blog and try to test this feature on https://github.com/elastic/elasticsearch main branch. https://www.elastic.co/search-labs/blog/knn-filter-post-filtering When a nested kNN query filters on a parent field, `KnnQueryUtils.computeSelectivity()` uses a parent-document iterator cost as the numerator and the child-vector count as the denominator. This systematically underestimates vector-document filter coverage in the reproduction below. Setting `index.dense_vector.post_filter_selectivity_threshold` to `0.0` makes the issue consistently observable in my local tests: the estimator returns the parent-based cost on every repeated request. Reproducing the bug does not require waiting for a cache-state transition. The method sums `ScorerSupplier.cost()` across leaves and divides by the number of vectors. The parent-to-child join iterator reports its parent iterator's cost even though its output documents are children. ### Observed behavior The test data has one nested path, one vector per chunk, and the following distribution: | Parent type | Parent documents | Chunks per parent | Vector-bearing child documents | | --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | | a | 100 | 5 | 500 | | b | 500 | 10 | 5,000 | | c | 2,000 | 20 | 40,000 | | Total | 2,600 | — | 45,500 | For the parent filter `type=b` and a threshold of `0.0`, the observed values are: | Measurement | Numerator | Total vectors | Selectivity | | --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | | First request: reported parent-based cost | 500 | 45,500 | 0.010989 (~1.10%) | | Repeated requests: reported parent-based cost | 500 | 45,500 | 0.010989 (~1.10%) | | Actual matching vector-child population | 5,000 | 45,500 | 0.109890 (~10.99%) | The estimate is ten times lower than vector-document coverage for type b because each matching parent has ten vector-bearing children. The repeated parent-cost result is the observation from this zero-threshold test; it is not a claim that setting the threshold to zero disables query caching in all configurations. ### Expected behavior The numerator and denominator should refer to the same population. If the denominator is the target field's vector count, the numerator should estimate matching vector-bearing child documents rather than inherit the parent iterator's execution cost. For this dataset, vector-document filter coverage is `5000 / 45500`. An inexpensive approximation is reasonable, but systematically substituting the number of matching parents for the number of matching vector children introduces a chunk-count-dependent bias. This report does not assume that corpus-level child coverage is an exact predictor of the survival rate of diversified nearest-neighbor candidates. ### Impact With a threshold of `0.0`, the incorrect estimate passes the post-filter gate and is then used for candidate expansion. Setting the threshold to zero exposes the issue consistently; it does not correct the estimate. A value of approximately 1.10% instead of 10.99% can substantially inflate the candidate target, subject to the expansion formula's floor and cap. At a nonzero threshold, the underestimate can also affect whether post-filtering is attempted. This report establishes an estimator discrepancy; it does not claim proven incorrect search hits, a measured tenfold increase in work, or a quantified latency regression. ### Steps to Reproduce The zero-threshold behavior described above was observed in local testing. The following is a compact reproduction recipe based on that dataset. **These exact commands have not yet been executed end to end as part of preparing this draft.** The generated data distribution has been checked separately. Replace this note with actual run results after validating the packaged recipe. Use an isolated development instance, a new index, one primary shard and no replicas. Keep profiling disabled so it does not change normal query-cache behavior; use debugger breakpoints/logpoints to observe the estimator. The examples assume an unsecured development endpoint at `http://localhost:9200`; adapt connection/authentication options to the test instance. ### 1. Create the test index This requires the development-build prerequisite described above. A private-setting error on a stock build is expected and does not reproduce this estimator issue. ```bash curl --fail-with-body -X PUT 'http://localhost:9200/nested-knn-selectivity-repro' \ -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{ "settings": { "number_of_shards": 1, "number_of_replicas": 0, "refresh_interval": "-1", "index.queries.cache.enabled": true, "index.dense_vector.post_filter_selectivity_threshold": 0.0 }, "mappings": { "properties": { "type": { "type": "keyword" }, "chunks": { "type": "nested", "properties": { "vector": { "type": "dense_vector", "element_type": "float", "dims": 4, "index": true, "similarity": "l2_norm", "index_options": { "type": "hnsw" } } } } } } }' ``` ### 2. Generate and index the documents The seeded generator deliberately makes vectors independent of parent type. It creates exactly 2,600 parent documents and 45,500 vector-bearing children. ```bash python3 - <<'PY' import json import random rng = random.Random(42) with open("nested-knn-bulk.ndjson", "w", encoding="utf-8") as out: for kind, parents, chunks in [("a", 100, 5), ("b", 500, 10), ("c", 2000, 20)]: for i in range(parents): action = {"create": {"_id": f"{kind}-{i}"}} doc = { "type": kind, "chunks": [ {"vector": [round(rng.uniform(-1, 1), 6) for _ in range(4)]} for _ in range(chunks) ], } out.write(json.dumps(action, separators=(",", ":")) + "\n") out.write(json.dumps(doc, separators=(",", ":")) + "\n") PY curl --fail-with-body -X POST \ 'http://localhost:9200/nested-knn-selectivity-repro/_bulk' \ -H 'Content-Type: application/x-ndjson' \ --data-binary @nested-knn-bulk.ndjson > nested-knn-bulk-response.json python3 - <<'PY' import json with open("nested-knn-bulk-response.json", encoding="utf-8") as src: response = json.load(src) assert response.get("errors") is False, response assert len(response["items"]) == 2600 print("Indexed 2,600 parents successfully") PY curl --fail-with-body -X POST \ 'http://localhost:9200/nested-knn-selectivity-repro/_refresh' curl --fail-with-body -X POST \ 'http://localhost:9200/nested-knn-selectivity-repro/_forcemerge?max_num_segments=1' curl --fail-with-body \ 'http://localhost:9200/nested-knn-selectivity-repro/_segments' ``` Confirm the primary has one searchable segment with 48,100 Lucene documents (2,600 parents + 45,500 children) and no deletions. issue.body:
The `Index Sort` test force merges to a single segment and then checks `_doc` order, which only works if the copy we search is actually that one merged segment. The health check after creating the index waits for no initializing shards, but that also passes while the replica is still unassigned. If the replica then gets assigned while we are indexing, it can still be recovering when the force merge runs, the merge skips it, and a search that lands on it returns docs out of index sort order (1,2,4,3 in the failure). This shows up mostly in the mixed cluster BWC runs since there are 4 nodes and more room for the replica to be late.

I first pinned `number_of_replicas: 0` like #160246 did for `340_flattened`, but that breaks serverless: stateless needs a replica to search on, so every search failed with no shard available (`340_flattened` only got away with it because serverless skips that test). 

So instead the index uses `auto_expand_replicas: 0-1` and the health check also waits for green. That gives

issue.title: ES|QL: EMBEDDING fails with a server error when its input is a constant held in a ROW/EVAL variable

labels.name: repo-51e13d60
labels.description: A label for assessing bug priority to be used by ES engineers

labels.name: repo-51e13d60
labels.description: Meta label for the Search Relevance team in Elasticsearch

labels.name: user-218bca2a/repo-29dda8c3
labels.description: Search functionality in ES|QL

issue.body:
## Summary

`EMBEDDING` throws `QlIllegalArgumentException: Should not fold expression` when its text or inference-id argument is a variable that holds a constant. The user gets a server error. `TEXT_EMBEDDING` rejects the same query during analysis with a clear message.

Found while working on #161305, assisted by 🤖 .

## Steps to reproduce

Either query fails. I reproduced both as `CsvIT` specs against `test_embedding_inference`:

```
ROW input="Who is Victor Hugo?"
| EVAL embedding = EMBEDDING(input, "test_embedding_inference")
```

```
ROW a = 1
| EVAL t = "Who is Victor Hugo?"
| EVAL embedding = EMBEDDING(t, "test_embedding_inference")
| KEEP t, embedding
```

## What happens

The query fails with `QlIllegalArgumentException: Should not fold expression`. That exception is documented as a server error, meant for bugs. Stack trace (line numbers from main at `7865babebf98`):

```
QlIllegalArgumentException: Should not fold expression
  at Expression.fold(Expression.java:101)
  at Literal.of(Literal.java:209)
  at RuleUtils.collectFoldableRefs(RuleUtils.java:157)
  at RuleUtils.foldableReferencesSkipMVGroupings(RuleUtils.java:122)
  at PropagateEvalFoldables.apply(PropagateEvalFoldables.java:34)
  at LogicalPlanOptimizer.optimize(LogicalPlanOptimizer.java:158)
  at EsqlSession.optimizedPlan(EsqlSession.java:3055)
```

`TEXT_EMBEDDING` with the same shape fails cleanly during analysis:

```
first argument of [TEXT_EMBEDDING(text, "text-embedding-inference-id")] must be a constant, received [text]
```

## What should happen

The query should work, or it should fail with a validation error. A server error is wrong either way.

## Why it happens

1. `Embedding.resolveType()` does not check foldability, so analysis accepts the variable.
2. `FoldInferenceFunctions` runs in the pre-optimizer, before the logical optimizer. It folds only functions that are already `foldable()`. `EMBEDDING(input, …)` is not, so it is skipped.
3. In the optimizer, `PropagateEvalFoldables` calls `RuleUtils.collectFoldableRefs`. That method substitutes known constants into each alias. The `Embedding` is now foldable, so it calls `Literal.of(...)`.
4. `Literal.of` calls `Embedding.fold()`. `Embedding` has no `fold()`, because inference calls run asynchronously through `FoldInferenceFunctions`. The default implementation throws.

Inline literals work, because the `Embedding` is already foldable when the pre-optimizer runs. Every existing `EMBEDDING` spec passes its text inline, even the specs with a `ROW` source. That is why nothing caught this.

## Why `EMBEDDING` checks after optimization

`Embedding` checks constants in `postOptimizationVerification`. `TEXT_EMBEDDING` checks in `resolveType()` with `isFoldable`. This behavior has been present since EMBEDDING was added in #144484. [Comments in that PR](https://github.com/elastic/elasticsearch/pull/144484/changes#r2980001766) suggest a unified approach between EMBEDDING and TEXT_EMBEDDING, but that is deferred for future work.

## Possible fixes

1. **Check foldability in `Embedding.resolveType()`, like `TEXT_EMBEDDING`.** This is a small change and gives the unified approach asked for in #144484. Variables get a clear error, and nothing that works today stops working. `VerifierTests.testEmbeddingLiteralValues` (which accepts a `ROW` attribute) and the `OptimizerVerificationTests` cases would need updating.
2. **Make deferral work.** Run `FoldInferenceFunctions` after constant propagation, and stop `collectFoldableRefs` from folding inference functions. This is a larger change to the optimizer pipeline.

Starting with the first option as a targeted fix and following up with the second as a longer term improvement seems like a reasonable progression.

issue.body:
QSTR documents a `fields` option but rejects it, e.g. `QSTR("hello", {"fields": ["title"]})` fails with `Invalid option [fields]`.

Allowing the key isn't enough on its own. The generic options handling turns every value into a single string, and `translate()` never passes any fields to the query, so `fields` is now read separately from the option literal and set as the fields of the `query_string` query.

How it behaves:
- `fields` takes a list or a single string, e.g. `{"fields": ["title^2", "desc*"]}` or `{"fields": "title"}`. Boosts and wildcards work the same as in the DSL (same parser).
- `fields` together with `default_field` is a verification error. The `query_string` query rejects that combination anyway, but only on the shard.
- Invalid or negative boosts (`title^high`, `title^-1`) are verification errors too.
- New `fn_qstr_fields_option` capability.

Tests: verifier tests for the accepted forms and the errors, a pushdown test checking the fields and boosts on the `QueryStringQueryBuilder`, csv-spec tests on `books` that only pass if `fields` is applied, and a check that every documented full-text `@MapParam` option is in `ALLOWED_OPTIONS`.

Closes #162643

issue.body:
The `Index Sort` test force merges to a single segment and then checks `_doc` order, which only works if the copy we search is actually that one merged segment. The health check after creating the index waits for no initializing shards, but that also passes while the replica is still unassigned. If the replica then gets assigned while we are indexing, it can still be recovering when the force merge runs, the merge skips it, and a search that lands on it returns docs out of index sort order (1,2,4,3 in the failure). This shows up mostly in the mixed cluster BWC runs since there are 4 nodes and more room for the replica to be late.

I first pinned `number_of_replicas: 0` like #160246 did for `340_flattened`, but that breaks serverless: stateless needs a replica to search on, so every search failed with no shard available (`340_flattened` only got away with it because serverless skips that test). 

So instead the index uses `auto_expand_replicas: 0-1` and the health check also waits for green. That gives 
- Single node: 0 replicas, so green is reachable.
- Multi-node: 1 replica, which must be started before indexing, so the force merge reaches both copies.
- Serverless: always at least 1 replica (AutoExpandReplicas.java:160), so searches have a shard again.

`30_multi_value` has the same setup and was muted for the same kind of failure, made the same change for that along with the unmutes (#154602, #161280, #163014).

`40_high_cardinality` and `340_flattened` get the same change, as a precaution and to keep the setup consistent.

>  Testing:  
>- The race didn't reproduce on its own locally (100 iterations with the failure seed), so I forced it with a scratch copy of the test: hold the replica back until after the health check, flush a large doc and throttle recovery so it's still running during the force merge. With the old health check it failed 5/5 with the same 1,2,4,3 order as CI, with the new one it passed 5/5.
> - `:rest-api-spec:yamlRestTest` for `indices.sort`, and `:qa:mixed-cluster:v9.3.8#yamlRestTest` for `Index Sort` (20 iterations).
> - Serverless `:qa:core-rest-test:yamlRestTest` and `yamlRestTestWithMultiProject` for `indices.sort` against this branch: the 5 no shard available failures from CI before the change, all green after (10 iterations).


The mute for this test only exists on 9.5 (#162592), so the backport should remove it there.

Closes #162591
Closes #154602
Closes #161280
Closes #163014

issue.body:
The `fields` option of ES|QL `QSTR` is documented but rejected at verification time.

{"index":{}}
{"title":"hello world","body":"foo"}

POST _query

Response (400):

verification_exception: line 1:21: Invalid option [fields] in [QSTR("hello", {"fields": ["title"]})], expected one of [analyzer, enable_position_increments, fuzzy_transpositions, fuzziness, default_operator, fuzzy_max_expansions, analyze_wildcard, rewrite, minimum_should_match, default_field, phrase_slop, boost, fuzzy_prefix_length, time_zone, allow_leading_wildcard, quote_analyzer, quote_field_suffix, max_determinized_states, auto_generate_synonyms_phrase_query, lenient]

A plain string value (`"fields": "title"`) fails the same way.

### Expected

`fields` is accepted and forwarded to the query string query.

issue.body:
The `vectordb_columnar.usage` test feature was only registered in `XPackFeatures#getTestFeatures` when the vectordb_columnar feature flag was on.
The idea was that the yaml test would skip on builds without the flag, but the yaml runner checks `cluster_features` against the feature metadata generated at build time and throws "Unknown feature" for anything it doesn't know about, rather than skipping. So with `-Dbuild.snapshot=false` the test failed every time.

This PR 
- always registers `vectordb_columnar.usage` as a test feature and the yaml test additionally requires the `vectordb_columnar_index_mode` capability on `PUT /{index}`, which is already advertised only when the flag is on (same thing `280_vectordb_columnar_index_mode.yml` does). 
- unmutes the test.

Tested locally with the repro line from the issue in release mode (`-Dbuild.snapshot=false -Dtests.jvm.argline=-Dbuild.snapshot=false`, like `release-tests.sh` does), where the test now gets skipped, and in a default snapshot run, where it runs and passes.

issue.title: Fix index sort yaml test race with replicas

labels.name: repo-51e13d60
labels.description: Issues or PRs that are addressing/adding tests

labels.name: repo-51e13d60
labels.description: Automatically create backport pull requests when merged

labels.name: repo-51e13d60

labels.name: user-218bca2a/repo-cee57863
labels.description: Catch all for Search Relevance

labels.name: user-67ce657a/repo-f7846dfc
labels.description: The label for issues and PRs related to columnar based index modes.

issue.body:
The `Index Sort` test force merges to a single segment and then checks `_doc` order, which only works if the copy we search is actually that one merged segment. The health check after creating the index waits for no initializing shards, but that also passes while the replica is still unassigned. If the replica then gets assigned while we are indexing, it can still be recovering when the force merge runs, the merge skips it, and a search that lands on it returns docs out of index sort order (1,2,4,3 in the failure). This shows up mostly in the mixed cluster BWC runs since there are 4 nodes and more room for the replica to be late.

I first pinned `number_of_replicas: 0` like #160246 did for `340_flattened`, but that breaks serverless: stateless needs a replica to search on, so every search failed with no shard available (`340_flattened` only got away with it because serverless skips that test). 

So instead the index uses `auto_expand_replicas: 0-1` and the health check also waits for green. That gives 
- Single node: 0 replicas, so green is reachable.
- Multi-node: 1 replica, which must be started before indexing, so the force merge reaches both copies.
- Serverless: always at least 1 replica (AutoExpandReplicas.java:160), so searches have a shard again.

`30_multi_value` has the same setup and was muted for the same kind of failure, made the same change for that along with the unmutes (#154602, #161280, #163014).

`40_high_cardinality` and `340_flattened` get the same change, as a precaution and to keep the setup consistent.

>  Testing:  
>- The race didn't reproduce on its own locally (100 iterations with the failure seed), so I forced it with a scratch copy of the test: hold the replica back until after the health check, flush a large doc and throttle recovery so it's still running during the force merge. With the old health check it failed 5/5 with the same 1,2,4,3 order as CI, with the new one it passed 5/5.
> - `:rest-api-spec:yamlRestTest` for `indices.sort`, and `:qa:mixed-cluster:v9.3.8#yamlRestTest` for `Index Sort` (20 iterations).
> - Serverless `:qa:core-rest-test:yamlRestTest` and `yamlRestTestWithMultiProject` for `indices.sort` against this branch: the 5 no shard available failures from CI before the change, all green after (10 iterations).


The mute for this test only exists on 9.5 (#162592), so the backport should remove it there.

Closes #162591
Closes #154602
Closes #161280
Closes #163014

### Repro line

```text

```

### Does it reproduce?

Yes

### Applicable branches

main

### Failure history

Started with #160018, which added the test. It fails on every release-tests (`-Dbuild.snapshot=false`) run. It reproduces locally on `main` @ 012d13b272df.

### Failure excerpt

```
XPackRestIT > test > test {yaml=vectordb_columnar/10_usage/vectordb_columnar usage} FAILED
    java.lang.IllegalArgumentException: Unknown feature vectordb_columnar.usage: check the respective FeatureSpecification is provided both in module-info.java as well as in META-INF/services and verify the module is loaded during tests.
        at org.elasticsearch.test.rest.ESRestTestFeatureService.clusterHasFeature(ESRestTestFeatureService.java:102)
        at org.elasticsearch.test.rest.yaml.ClientYamlTestExecutionContext.clusterHasFeature(ClientYamlTestExecutionContext.java:298)
        at org.elasticsearch.test.rest.yaml.section.Prerequisites.lambda$requireClusterFeatures$7(Prerequisites.java:45)
```

`XPackFeatures#getTestFeatures` only adds `vectordb_columnar.usage` when `IndexMode.VECTORDB_COLUMNAR_FEATURE_FLAG` is enabled. In release builds the flag is off, so the feature is unknown to the test runner. The `requires: cluster_features` check in `10_usage.yml` throws on an unknown feature instead of skipping the test.

issue.body:
The `Index Sort` test force merges to a single segment and then checks `_doc` order, which only works if the copy we search is actually that one merged segment. The health check after creating the index waits for no initializing shards, but that also passes while the replica is still unassigned. If the replica then gets assigned while we are indexing, it can still be recovering when the force merge runs, the merge skips it, and a search that lands on it returns docs out of index sort order (1,2,4,3 in the failure). This shows up mostly in the mixed cluster BWC runs since there are 4 nodes and more room for the replica to be late.

I first pinned `number_of_replicas: 0` like #160246 did for `340_flattened`, but that breaks serverless: stateless needs a replica to search on, so every search failed with no shard available (`340_flattened` only got away with it because serverless skips that test). 

So instead the index uses `auto_expand_replicas: 0-1` and the health check also waits for green. That gives 
- Single node: 0 replicas, so green is reachable.
- Multi-node: 1 replica, which must be started before indexing, so the force merge reaches both copies.
- Serverless: always at least 1 replica (AutoExpandReplicas.java:160), so searches have a shard again.

`30_multi_value` has the same setup and was muted for the same kind of failure, made the same change for that along with the unmutes (#154602, #161280, #163014).

`40_high_cardinality` and `340_flattened` get the same change, as a precaution and to keep the setup consistent.

>  Testing:  
>- The race didn't reproduce on its own locally (100 iterations with the failure seed), so I forced it with a scratch copy of the test: hold the replica back until after the health check, flush a large doc and throttle recovery so it's still running during the force merge. With the old health check it failed 5/5 with the same 1,2,4,3 order as CI, with the new one it passed 5/5.
> - `:rest-api-spec:yamlRestTest` for `indices.sort`, and `:qa:mixed-cluster:v9.3.8#yamlRestTest` for `Index Sort` (20 iterations).
> - Serverless `:qa:core-rest-test:yamlRestTest` and `yamlRestTestWithMultiProject` for `indices.sort` against this branch: the 5 no shard available failures from CI before the change, all green after (10 iterations).


The mute for this test only exists on 9.5 (#162592), so the backport should remove it there.

Closes #162591
Closes #154602
Closes #161280
Closes #163014
